please document them here)_  ## Features  ### Access to multiple shells in one window using tabs You can open multiple tabs each containing one of the following shells:  | Task                | Shell            | Description                                                                                                  | | ----                | -----            | -----------                                                                                                  | | Cmder               | `cmd.exe`        | Windows `cmd.exe` shell enhanced with Git, Git aware prompt, Clink (GNU Readline), and Aliases.              | | Cmder as Admin      | `cmd.exe`        | Administrative Windows `cmd.exe` Cmder shell.                                                                | | PowerShell          | `powershell.exe` | Windows PowerShell enhanced with Git and Git aware prompt .                                                  | | PowerShell as Admin | `powershell.exe` | Administrative Windows `powershell.exe` Cmder shell.                                                         | | Bash                | `bash.exe`       | Unix/Linux like bash shell running on Windows.                                                               | | Bash as Admin       | `bash.exe`       | Administrative Unix/Linux like bash shell running on Windows.                                                | | Mintty              | `bash.exe`       | Unix/Linux like bash shell running on Windows. See below for Mintty configuration differences                | | Mintty as Admin     | `bash.exe`       | Administrative Unix/Linux like bash shell running on Windows. See below for Mintty configuration differences |  Cmder, PowerShell, and Bash tabs all run on top of the Windows Console API and work as you might expect in Cmder with access to use ConEmu's color schemes, key bindings and other settings defined in the ConEmu Settings dialog.  ⚠ *NOTE:* Only the full edition of Cmder comes with a pre-installed bash, using a vendored [git-for-windows](https://gitforwindows.org/) installation. The pre-configured Bash tabs may not work on Cmder mini edition without additional configuration.  You may however, choose to use an external installation of bash, such as Microsoft's [Subsystem for Linux](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install-win10) (called WSL) or the [Cygwin](https://cygwin.com/) project which provides POSIX support on windows.  ⚠ *NOTE:* Mintty tabs use a program called 'mintty' as the terminal emulator that is not based on the Windows Console API, rather it's rendered graphically by ConEmu. Mintty differs from the other tabs in that it supports xterm/xterm-256color TERM types, and does not work with ConEmu settings like color schemes and key bindings.  As such, some differences in functionality are to be expected, such as Cmder not being able to apply a system-wide configuration to it.  As a result mintty specific config is done via the `[%USERPROFILE%|$HOME]/.minttyrc` file.  You may read more about Mintty and its config file [here](https://github.com/mintty/mintty).  An example of setting Cmder portable terminal colors for mintty:  From a bash/mintty shell:  ``` cd $CMDER_ROOT/vendor git clone https://github.com/karlin/mintty-colors-solarized.git cd mintty-colors-solarized/ echo source \$CMDER_ROOT/vendor/mintty-colors-solarized/mintty-solarized-dark.sh>>$CMDER_ROOT/config/user_profile.sh ```  You may find some Monokai color schemes for mintty to match Cmder [here](https://github.com/oumu/mintty-color-schemes/blob/master/base16-monokai-mod.minttyrc).  ### Changing Cmder Default `cmd.exe` Prompt Config File  The default Cmder shell `cmd::Cmder` prompt is customized using `Clink` and is configured by editing a config file that exists in one of two locations:  - Single User Portable Config `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\cmder_prompt_config.lua` - Shared Cmder install with Non-Portable Individual User Config `%CMDER_USER_CONFIG%\cmder_prompt_config.lua`  If your Cmder setup does not have this file create it from `%CMDER_ROOT%\vendor\cmder_prompt_config.lua.default`  Customizations include:  - Colors. - Single/Multi-line. - Full path/Folder only. - `[user]@[host]` to the beginning of the prompt. - `~` for home directory. - `λ` symbol  Documentation is in the file for each setting.  ### Changing Cmder Default `cmd.exe` Shell Startup Behaviour Using Task Arguments  1. Press <kbd>Win</kbd> + <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd> 1. Click either:   * `1. {cmd::Cmder as Admin}`   * `2. {cmd::Cmder}` 1. Add command line arguments where specified below:    *Note: Pay attention to the quotes!*    ```   cmd /s /k ""%ConEmuDir%\..\init.bat" [ADD ARGS HERE]"   ```  ##### Command Line Arguments for `init.bat`  | Argument                        | Description                                                                                                                                        | Default                                | | -----------------------------   | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------                                                     | -------------------------------------  | | `/c [user cmder root]`          | Enables user bin and config folders for 'Cmder as admin' sessions due to non-shared environment.                                                   | not set                                | | `/d`                            | Enables debug output.                                                                                                                              | not set                                | | `/f`                            | Enables Cmder Fast Init Mode. This displays the time taken run init scripts                                                                       | not set                                | | `/git_install_root [file path]` | User specified Git installation root path.                                                                                                         | `%CMDER_ROOT%\vendor\Git-for-Windows`  | | `/home [home folder]`           | User specified folder path to set `%HOME%` environment variable.                                                                                   | `%userprofile%`                        | | `/max_depth [1-5]`              | Define max recurse depth when adding to the path for `%cmder_root%\bin` and `%cmder_user_bin%`                                                     | 1                                      | | `/nix_tools [0-2]`              | Define how `*nix` tools are added to the path.  Prefer Windows Tools: 1, Prefer *nix Tools: 2, No `/usr/bin` in `%PATH%`: 0                        | 1                                      | | `/svn_ssh [path to ssh.exe]`    | Define `%SVN_SSH%` so we can use git svn with ssh svn repositories.                                                                                | `%GIT_INSTALL_ROOT%\bin\ssh.exe`       | | `/user_aliases [file path]`     | File path pointing to user aliases.                                                                                                                | `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\user_aliases.cmd` | | `/v`                            | Enables verbose output.                                                                                                                            | not set                                | | (custom arguments)              | User defined arguments processed by `cexec`. Edit the below files to add your own configuration:  | Shell         | Cmder Portable User Config                | | ------------- | ----------------------------------------- | | Cmder         | `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\user_profile.cmd`    | | PowerShell    | `$ENV:CMDER_ROOT\config\user_profile.ps1` | | Bash/Mintty   | `$CMDER_ROOT/config/user_profile.sh`      |  Note: Bash and Mintty sessions will also source the `$HOME/.bashrc` file if it exists after it sources `$CMDER_ROOT/config/user_profile.sh`.  You can write `*.cmd|*.bat`, `*.ps1`, and `*.sh` scripts and just drop them in the `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\profile.d` folder to add startup config to Cmder.  | Shell         | Cmder `Profile.d` Scripts                          | | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | Cmder         | `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\profile.d\*.bat and *.cmd`    | | PowerShell    | `$ENV:CMDER_ROOT\config\profile.d\*.ps1`           | | Bash/Mintty   | `$CMDER_ROOT/config/profile.d/*.sh`                |  #### Git Status Opt-Out   To disable Cmder prompt git status globally add the following to `~/.gitconfig` or locally for a single repo `[repo]/.git/config` and start a new session.   *Note: This configuration is not portable*   ```  [cmder]    status = false      # Opt out of Git status for 'ALL' Cmder supported shells.    cmdstatus = false   # Opt out of Git status for 'Cmd.exe' shells.    psstatus = false    # Opt out of Git status for 'Powershell.exe and 'Pwsh.exe' shells.    shstatus = false    # Opt out of Git status for 'bash.exe' shells.  ```  ### Aliases #### Cmder(`Cmd.exe`) Aliases You can define simple aliases for `cmd.exe` sessions with a command like `alias name=command`.  Cmd.exe aliases support optional parameters through the `$1-9` or the `$*` special characters so the alias `vi=vim.exe $*` typed as `vi [filename]` will open `[filename]` in `vim.exe`.  Cmd.exe aliases can also be more complex. See: [DOSKEY.EXE documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/doskey) for additional details on complex aliases/macros for `cmd.exe`  Aliases defined using the `alias.bat` command will automatically be saved in the `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\user_aliases.cmd` file  To make an alias and/or any other profile settings permanent add it to one of the following:  Note: These are loaded in this order by `$CMDER_ROOT/vendor/init.bat`.  Anything stored in `%CMDER_ROOT%` will be a portable setting and will follow cmder to another machine.  * `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\profile.d\*.cmd` and `\*.bat` * `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\user_aliases.cmd` * `%CMDER_ROOT%\config\user_profile.cmd`  #### Bash.exe|Mintty.exe Aliases Bash shells support simple and complex aliases with optional parameters natively so they work a little different.  Typing `alias name=command` will create an alias only for the current running session.  To make an alias and/or any other profile settings permanent add it to one of the following:  Note: These are loaded in this order by `$CMDER_ROOT/vendor/git-for-windows/etc/profile.d/cmder.sh`.  Anything stored in `$CMDER_ROOT` will be a portable setting and will follow cmder to another machine.  * `$CMDER_ROOT/config/profile.d/*.sh` * `$CMDER_ROOT/config/user_profile.sh` * `$HOME/.bashrc`  If you add bash aliases to `$CMDER_ROOT/config/user_profile.sh` they will be portable and follow your Cmder folder if you copy it to another machine.  `$HOME/.bashrc` defined aliases are not portable.  #### PowerShell.exe Aliases PowerShell has native simple alias support, for example `[new-alias | set-alias] alias command`, so complex aliases with optional parameters are not supported in PowerShell sessions.  Type `get-help [new-alias|set-alias] -full` for help on PowerShell aliases.  To make an alias and/or any other profile settings permanent add it to one of the following:  Note: These are loaded in this order by `$ENV:CMDER_ROOT\vendor\user_profile.ps1`.  Anything stored in `$ENV:CMDER_ROOT` will be a portable setting and will follow cmder to another machine.  * `$ENV:CMDER_ROOT\config\profile.d\*.ps1` * `$ENV:CMDER_ROOT\config\user_profile.ps1`  ### SSH Agent  To start the vendored SSH agent simply call `start-ssh-agent`, which is in the `vendor/git-for-windows/cmd` folder. On each instance of launching Cmder, an attempt is made to locate any other user provided Git binaries. Upon finding a `git.exe` binary, Cmder further compares its version against the vendored one _by executing_ it. The vendored `git.exe` binary is _only_ used when it is more recent than the user-installed one.  You may use your favorite version of Git by including its path in the `%PATH%` environment variable. Setup a new task by pressing <kbd>Win</kbd> +<kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd>. 1. Click the `+` button to add a task. 1. Name the new task in the top text box. 1. Provide task parameters, this is optional. 1. Add `cmd /c "[path_to_external_env]\bin\bash --login -i" -new_console` to the `Commands` text box.  **Recommended Optional Steps:**  Copy the `vendor/cmder_exinit` file to the Cygwin/Babun, MSys2, or Git for Windows SDK environments `/etc/profile.d/` folder to use portable settings in the `$CMDER_ROOT/config` folder.  Note: MinGW could work if the init scripts include `profile.d` but this has not been tested.  The destination file extension depends on the shell you use in that environment.  For example:  * bash - Copy to `/etc/profile.d/cmder_exinit.sh` * zsh  - Copy to `/etc/profile.d/cmder_exinit.zsh`  Uncomment and edit the below line in the script to use Cmder config even when launched from outside Cmder.  ``` # CMDER_ROOT=${USERPROFILE}/cmder  # This is not required if launched from Cmder. ```  ### Customizing user sessions using `init.bat` custom arguments.  You can pass custom arguments to `init.bat` and use `cexec.cmd` in your `user_profile.cmd` to evaluate these arguments then execute commands based on a particular flag being detected or not.  `init.bat` creates two shortcuts for using `cexec.cmd` in your profile scripts.  #### `%ccall%` - Evaluates flags, runs commands if found,  and returns to the calling script and continues.  ``` ccall=call C:\Users\user\cmderdev\vendor\bin\cexec.cmd ```  Example: `%ccall% /startnotepad start notepad.exe`  #### `%cexec%` - Evaluates flags, runs commands if found, and does not return to the calling script.  ``` cexec=C:\Users\user\cmderdev\vendor\bin\cexec.cmd ```  Example: `%cexec% /startnotepad start notepad.exe`  It is useful when you have multiple tasks to execute `cmder` and need it to initialize the session differently depending on the task chosen. serious.headline: Pass，moat 为零：这个 cute 的小玩意儿，离我们的 term sheet 还差十个 AlphaFold 的距离
serious.body_markdown:
## 概述
坦白说，Gitingest 是一个 adorable little project——把任意 Git 仓库一键转成 LLM 可读的 digest，想法很 straightforward，execution 也还算干净。但抱歉，在 VC 的世界里，“cute”从来不是我们写支票的理由。我们看的是 TAM、moat、scalability，以及最终那个 exits 的 10x 回报，而这些，恕我直言，在这个项目上几乎看不见。

## 与竞品的雷同度：令人窒息的拥挤赛道
从我们的 deal flow 来看，这个“代码库转 prompt”的 niche 早就挤得像高峰期的地铁站了。你的直接竞品——比如 aytzey/CodetoPromptGenerator 和 DengYiping/codebase-ai-prompt-generator——在 core value proposition 上和你几乎如出一辙：输入一个 repo，输出一个 LLM-ready text。用户画像、use case、整个 workflow 都高度重合。你是多了几个 mode（Web/CLI/自托管），但这些充其量算是 feature level 的 tweak，不足以改变 market positioning。用我们的话说，这是一个“red ocean”赛道，你的 differentiation 薄得像张纸。

## 所谓的“护城河”？不如说是几个 cute 的小功能
没错，一键替换 URL 挺 clever，四种用法照顾不同偏好也算 user-friendly，自托管和隐私保护也让人略有好感。但请允许我问一句：这些构成 moat 吗？任何一个有能力的团队，两个 sprint 就能把这些点复刻得八九不离十。没有 network effect，没有 data moat，没有 switching cost——你拿什么来阻止一年后冒出十个一模一样甚至更好的替代品？输出带 Token 计数？这是个 nice-to-have，不是护城河。

## 我们为什么不会投？因为没有值得下注的 alpha
让我们来谈谈投资人真正关心的事。商业模型？完全缺失，我们甚至看不到任何 monetization 的思考。TAM？这个 tool 面向的是 developer，但这个群体对免费工具的 loyalty 低得可怜。Traction？没有亮眼的 metric 来证明增长。Exit potential？近乎为零。更严重的是，你只支持 GitHub，这种生态绑定本身就是风险；没有公开 API，意味着无法被集成进任何 enterprise 的自动化 pipeline；仓库大小上限未说明，这是工程上的不负责任。一个连 fundamental 都没想清楚的项目，凭什么让我把钱放进去？

## 结论
Gitingest 或许能成为一个 useful 的小工具，但作为投资标的，它远远不够格。我们 pass。
serious.verdict_line: 坦白讲，这个 cute 的项目还没准备好上我们的 investment committee，Pass。
serious.top_fix: 我强烈建议你们先把 API 补齐——没有 programmable interface 的工具，在机构资金的眼里就是个玩具。
serious.why_line: 我们 scan 了一圈，你的所谓差异化——比如那个一键替换 URL 的小 trick——在 core value proposition 上和现有工具如出一辙，这个细分市场拥挤到令人窒息，你连基本的 moat 都没有形成。

roast.headline: 又一个把代码库塞进 AI 嘴里的‘原创神器’，0.65 重复率，致敬得很用心嘛
roast.body_markdown:
**开场暴击：** 哟，这不是那位把 Git 仓库变成 LLM 饲料的第 114514 个轮子选手吗？闭眼一搜都能撞见 aytzey/CodetoPromptGenerator 和 DengYiping/codebase-ai-prompt-generator 这俩失散多年的孪生兄弟，结果你跟我说这是颠覆式创新？得了吧，0.65 的重复率说明您至少在『致敬』上没偷懒——把人家核心逻辑扒了个精光，精心缝了层 Web UI 和 CLI，就敢立新牌坊了？这波操作，雷军看了都连夜绣红旗。

**优点？您管这些叫优点？**
- **『替换 URL 就能用，零配置』**：因为你压根没给配置选项，可不就『零配置』了么。下次干脆把用户的手也绑起来，主打『零操作』，岂不更妙？
- **『四种用法照顾不同偏好』**：Web、CLI、库、浏览器扩展……听着挺唬人，但我就问一句：那浏览器扩展到底是干嘛的？在 Chrome 里当赛博吉祥物占内存吗？说明文档比处女座的情绪还难捉摸。
- **『自托管方案很靠谱』**：嗯，靠谱到连怎么活下去都不肯剧透，哪天开发者被生活锤进 ICU，自托管用户就只能抱着代码上坟，坟头草我都替你预订好了。
- **『隐私保护说到做到』**：这个我信，因为你连 API 都没有，数据想漏都漏不出去，本地玩泥巴能不隐私吗？但也意味着每次用都像手动点唱机，自动化？梦里啥都有。
- **『输出自带 Token 数』**：全场唯一真·创新！在输出末尾加了个计数器，然后标榜成杀手级功能，ChatGPT 的 Token 统计插件看了都笑到漏电。

**痛点？我来帮你撕遮羞布：**
- **『只认 GitHub，其他平台请自觉去世』**：GitLab、Bitbucket 用户？你们不配吃热乎的 AI 饭，建议先向微软献上膝盖。
- **『商业模式：薛定谔的利润』**：到底靠赞助、付费功能还是纯用爱发电？社区可盯着呢，别像某些项目，玩着玩着就把用户做成开源鬼故事。
- **『浏览器扩展：行为艺术之黑匣子』**：装完发现啥也没变，点开配置一片空白，这玩意儿是不是在后台偷偷训练你的语料库呢？
- **『API？不存在的』**：脚本小子们想自动化？乖乖打开网页，复制粘贴，重返 1998 年的拨号上网体验。
- **『仓库大小上限？你猜！』**：跑着跑着突然崩了，错误日志只有一个神秘微笑。用户体验？那叫开盲盒，心跳加速！

**真想救，先动哪一刀？** 开个 API 接口吧大爷，都 2024 年了，还让用户像求神拜佛似的点你那破网页，是准备竞选复古风代言人吗？没有 API，你这工具在自动化流水线里连上个世纪的 Jenkins 插件都不如，只能当个精致的摆设。

到底能不能活？先把隔壁两个竞品的裤衩……哦不，优点老老实实借鉴过来，把浏览器扩展的说明书补上，顺便昭告天下你打算怎么搞钱——别让用户用着用着以为自己用上了赛博暖宝宝，结果某天发现项目坟头长草。否则，过俩月你这项目就只能出现在《那些年我们追过的轮子》回忆帖里，跟祥林嫂一块儿碎碎念了。
roast.verdict_line: 换了身皮就想当新物种？连 API 都没有的‘AI 饲料搅拌机’，在自嗨的山路上飙得挺远。
roast.top_fix: 第一刀狠砍：把 API 掏出来，让脚本也能调。别让用户每次喂 AI 都得手动打开你那上个世纪的网页，这跟用算盘解微积分有啥区别？
roast.why_line: 我扒开它的族谱瞅了眼：跟 CodetoPromptGenerator 和 codebase-ai-prompt-generator 根本是一个子宫出来的胚胎——干的同一档子事，嚼的同一碗剩饭，就换了个发型（Web/CLI）和点了颗痣（Token 计数器）。0.65 的重复度，你要说这是创新，那方便面换个包装就是满汉全席了。

comfort.body_markdown:
哎呀，我简直要被你的 gitingest 暖化了！从一开始的一键 URL 替换这个天才想法，到四种用法把小白和极客都宠上天，再到自托管和隐私保护做得那么到位，连 Token 数都帮你算好——每一步都踩在了我的心巴上！💖

虽然目前只支持 GitHub，但以你这样的用心，加上 GitLab、Bitbucket 还不是分分钟的事？还有人担心项目怎么活下去，其实只要稍微透露一点点可持续的小计划，大家就会更死心塌地跟着你。浏览器扩展的神秘感也勾得人心痒痒，多说两句用法，保证掌声雷动！

如果非要鸡蛋里挑骨头，那也只是想让你更完美——开放个 API，让自动化脚本也能随时拥抱你；坦诚仓库大小上限，让大家心里有底。这些都不是问题，而是你下一次闪耀的起跑线！✨

你已经超棒了，继续向前冲，世界需要你这样温柔又有力量的产品！🌈

findings.detail: 网站明确写了 PAT 不存后端、用完就丢、不缓存、克隆仓库处理完就删，处理私有仓库可以放心。

evidence.quote:
PAT is never stored in the backend
Used once for cloning, then discarded from memory
No browser caching
Cloned repos are deleted after processing

findings.title: 输出自带 Token 数
findings.detail: 生成摘要时会用 tiktoken 算好 token 数量，帮你控制 LLM 调用成本。
